Evaluating jihoo: Lessons for sci > jihoo Measured: Bootstrap, Speed, Verification

jihoo Measured: Bootstrap, Speed, Verification

jihoo is a small systems language whose compiler (53,489 lines of jihoo) combines a borrow checker, a compile-time proof engine that deletes runtime checks, and an LLVM backend. Because sci — the SA compiler underneath SLA — is currently bottlenecked on performance, jihoo was evaluated hands-on as a source of borrowable engineering: what it does, what it costs, and what of it sci can adopt. This chapter records the measured results and the adoption assessment. Everything below was run on 2026-11-27 against jihoo HEAD 5f18751de4e80bc09f62a9899f8d66b5641fb9a1 (version 0.6.0, bootstrapped from the bundled v0.5.0 seed).

Isolation. The evaluation ran in a dedicated directory on an 8-core host, with LLVM 21.1.8 unpacked into an isolated prefix (no system install, no global PATH or linker changes). The sci tree was not touched; the point was to learn from jihoo, not to disturb the production compiler.

Bootstrap: a reached fixed point

StageWall clockResult
Seed 0.5.0 compiles compiler/63.89 sstage1, reports jihoo 0.6.0
stage1 compiles compiler/63.05 sstage2, reports jihoo 0.6.0

stage1 and stage2 are byte-identical (sha256 caa942d2…, 2,804,192 bytes each): the self-hosting bootstrap reaches its fixed point. Smoke test: jihoo run examples/hello.jh prints Hello, jihoo!.

Runtime speed: 94–98% of C

The official functional-fusion benchmark (size 1,000,000, medians of 7 repeats, same harness, C reference compiled by clang -O2):

ImplementationTimeRatio vs CAllocations/call
C reference (clang -O2)0.048292 s1.0000
jihoo iterator combinators0.049073 s1.0160
jihoo functional combinators0.051345 s1.0630
jihoo handwritten loop0.051865 s1.0740
jihoo staged0.052092 s1.0790
jihoo eager (unfused baseline)0.717586 s14.85937

Machine-code evidence: the functional, staged and handwritten function bodies are byte-identical (144 bytes each) — combinator code is fully fused down to the same code as a handwritten loop, with zero allocation. The unfused eager form shows what fusion is worth: 14.9× slower and 37 allocations per call.

Compile speed: the frontend is 3%

Workloadcheck (frontend only)full (-O2)
compiler (all 53,489 lines)1.952 s62.951 s
comptime0.153 s0.778 s
format0.210 s1.325 s
fusion kernels0.020 s0.213 s

Checking the entire compiler takes about 2 seconds; the remaining ~97% of a full build is LLVM optimization and code generation. The structural lesson (frontend share ≈ 3%) transfers even though the absolute numbers do not — jihoo's language surface and compiler are much smaller than sci's.

Verification: a third of all checks proved away

jihoo verify on its own compiler plus std instances (4,960 functions) finishes in 19.059 s and proves 1,761 of 7,597 checks: bounds and overflow checks 1,544 / 4,624 (33.4%), potentially panicking calls 217 / 2,424, panics 0 / 549. Unproved checks are kept, each with a stated reason. Verification runs by default on every build (--no-verify disables it), so the 63-second bootstrap above already includes its cost. How the proof engine works — and why it is the single most valuable thing for sci to borrow — is the next page.

Sources: jihoolang/jihoo HEAD 5f18751de4e80bc09f62a9899f8d66b5641fb9a1 (0.6.0); seed package sha256 a9fedcae…3134ecadc, matching the value pinned in bootstrap/README.md. All numbers measured 2026-11-27 on an 8-core host with LLVM 21.1.8 in an isolated prefix; sci sources untouched. Full evaluation record: jihoo-bench RESULT (sha256 ccb30ebbc36bd049…).
